sourcedFrom: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: A 1301 built for competition arrives assembled and is expected to keep running through a programme, not a morning. The strip is the same tool-free sequence the rest of Beretta's semiautos use — cap, fore-end, barrel, bolt group — and the same hard rule governs the gas system: clean it, then put it back dry.

steps.title: Three places checked, hammer decocked
steps.action: Ejection port, loading gate, chamber — look at each one, then confirm the hammer is decocked. A competition gun gets handled between stations more than it gets fired, which is exactly why the check happens every time and not just at the end.
steps.aside: It is advisable to carry out the stripping operations over a table to catch components should they drop.
steps.quote: ALWAYS CHECK THAT THE SHOTGUN IS UNLOADED (EMPTY CARTRIDGE CHAMBER, EMPTY RECEIVER, EMPTY MAGAZINE). INSPECT THE FIREARM BY LOOKING THROUGH THE EJECTION PORT, THE LOADING GATE AND THE CHAMBER. IF IT IS NOT EMPTY, UNLOAD IT AS INSTRUCTED IN THE RELEVANT SECTION. CHECK THAT THE HAMMER IS DECOCKED.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Carrier stop pin all the way down, bolt open
steps.action: Push the carrier stop pin fully down, then pull the bolt right back so it stays open. Nothing forward of the receiver will release until both of those are true, and the cap is not the part to force.
steps.aside: Pull the breech bolt all the way back so that it remains open
steps.quote: Check that the carrier stop pin is pressed all the way down. If it is not, push it all the way down
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Front cap anticlockwise, fore-end off toward the muzzle
steps.action: Unscrew the fore-end's front cap anticlockwise, then hold the gun by the BARREL and pull the fore-end straight out toward the muzzle. Straight is the whole trick — angled, it wedges on the magazine tube.
steps.aside: Holding the shotgun by the barrel, pull the fore-end straight out toward the muzzle.
steps.quote: Unscrew the front cap of the fore-end in an anticlockwise direction.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: ⛔ Barrel off with the piston held — and the valve stays shut
steps.action: Draw the barrel out of the stock-receiver assembly with the piston held inside its gas cylinder, then let the piston parts off the tube. ⛔ The valve is where this stops: never strip its spring or its retaining nut. It is self-cleaning and needs no maintenance; if it is genuinely wrong, that is a factory-trained gunsmith's work.
steps.aside: The valve device is self-cleaning and requires no maintenance
steps.quote: Pull the barrel out of the stock-receiver assembly while holding the piston inside the gas cylinder.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Bore, and then the locking shoulders
steps.action: Soft flannel through the bore, bronze brush or an oiled cloth for the rest, dry cloth after, then a light film. Then the breech end, and give it real attention — a competition gun that starts closing sluggishly halfway through a programme is usually complaining about those bearing surfaces, not about the shells.
steps.aside: Lightly lubricate the barrel with a soft clean cloth soaked with Beretta Gun Oil.
steps.quote: Thoroughly clean the locking shoulders on the barrel breech.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.35-36

steps.title: Gas system cleaned, then left dry
steps.action: Clean and spray the piston, the elastic piston seal and the magazine tube; spray the cylinder walls, brush them with a bronze brush and wipe the inside out. ⛔ Then stop — Beretta says the components named must not be lubricated, and a wet gas system is the fastest route to a gun that will not finish a round.
steps.aside: After removing any combustion residue, clean the inside of the gas cylinder with a clean cloth.
steps.quote: Carefully clean the piston, elastic piston seal and magazine tube and spray with Beretta Gun Oil.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.35-36

steps.title: Piston glides freely, or it does not go back
steps.action: Push the piston along the magazine tube by hand. It should slide with no catch at all. This is the check that separates a gun that will run a full programme from one that starts leaving the bolt short somewhere in the middle of it.
steps.aside: To clean the walls of the gas cylinder, spray them with Beretta Gun Oil and clean thoroughly with a bronze brush.
steps.quote: Ensure that the piston glides freely on the magazine tube.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.35-36

deepSteps.title: The bolt comes apart to be CLEANED, and for nothing else
deepSteps.action: Beretta puts the reason above the procedure, and it is the reason to do this at the end of a season rather than after a squad: the breech bolt assembly is taken down to clean its components. Nothing below is a tuning operation.
deepSteps.quote: The breech bolt assembly needs only to be disassembled in order to clean its components.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Ride the bolt forward under control
deepSteps.action: Keep the index or middle finger on the cocking handle, press the release button, and let the bolt travel forward slowly until it stops. Letting it slam is how a bolt face and a barrel breech get peened over a season of doing it.
deepSteps.quote: Keeping the index or middle finger of your left hand on the cocking handle, press the release button and allow the breech bolt to move forward slowly until it stops.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Depress the bolt head until the neck groove lines up
deepSteps.action: Press the head of the bolt in until the groove in its neck sits level with the edge of the bolt body. With the groove aligned the cocking handle will pull straight out and it takes force; with it misaligned nothing will come and levering it is how the handle gets bent.
deepSteps.aside: Keeping the head depressed in this position, extract the cocking handle from the breech bolt, pulling forcefully.
deepSteps.quote: Press the head of the breech bolt until the groove on its neck corresponds to the edge of the bolt body.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Bolt group forward off the receiver — ejection port UP
deepSteps.action: Flat surface, ejection port facing upward, and pull the bolt assembly, the operating rods with sleeve, the recoil spring and the spring holder forward together. Port up is what keeps the firing pin, the locking block and their springs inside the bolt instead of on the floor.
deepSteps.quote: Working over a flat surface, with the ejection port pointed upwards, pull forward on the breech bolt assembly, the operating rods with sleeve, the recoil spring, and the spring holder, to force the breech bolt out from the receiver
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate out — safety ON, hammer cocked
deepSteps.action: Engage the safety with the hammer cocked, press the carrier stop pin, then drive the trigger guard retaining pin out with a punch or an awl and lever the plate free by the trigger guard — toward the barrel first, then outward. The order matters; pulling straight out binds it.
deepSteps.aside: The trigger plate only needs to be disassembled in order to clean the trigger mechanism.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the trigger guard retaining pin by pressing with a pin punch or an awl.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Clean bolt, plate and receiver — then put the tools down
deepSteps.action: Spray and clean the bolt parts, dry them thoroughly, lubricate lightly. Wipe the trigger plate and put a light film on its metal parts and its retaining pin. Do the receiver the same way, lubricating the internal bolt guides. ⛔ The plate comes OUT to be cleaned; it does not come APART, and the valve stays exactly where the strip left it.
deepSteps.aside: Proceed as indicated for the breech bolt. Clean thoroughly with a soft cloth and lubricate the internal breech bolt guides.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly lubricate all the metal components and the trigger plate retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — SPECIAL MAINTENANCE, printed p.36

cleaning.name: BARREL & LOCKING SHOULDERS
tasks: Flannel through the bore for combustion residue; bronze brush if a match day has earned it
Locking shoulders at the barrel breech cleaned thoroughly
Dry cloth through, then a light oil; bore and chamber checked clear of obstruction

cleaning.name: GAS CYLINDER, PISTON, SEAL, MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Piston, elastic piston seal and magazine tube cleaned and sprayed
Piston proved to glide freely along the tube by hand
Cylinder walls sprayed and brushed, then wiped out with a clean cloth
⛔ These components must NOT be lubricated

cleaning.name: BREECH BOLT, TRIGGER PLATE, RECEIVER (end of season)
tasks: Bolt parts sprayed and cleaned, dried thoroughly, lightly lubricated
Trigger plate wiped; metal parts and the retaining pin lightly oiled
Receiver treated as the bolt was, internal bolt guides lubricated

cleaning.name: ⛔ LEAVE ALONE
tasks: The valve assembly is never disassembled
The valve spring and the valve retaining nut are never stripped
Oil never goes on a cartridge, and never stays in the bore

reassembly: Trigger plate back in with the hammer cocked and the safety engaged, rear of the plate flush to the receiver, pushed firmly toward the stock.
Retaining pin in only once the trigger guard hole is centred on the receiver.
Bolt group, operating rods with sleeve, recoil spring and piston stop onto the magazine tube, ejection port UP on a flat surface.
Bolt head depressed to the neck groove, cocking handle driven home firmly.
Piston into the barrel's gas cylinder, elastic seal pinched between the fingers to start it.
Barrel checked clear, carrier stop pin down, fore-end on and the front cap tightened.
fncheck: Back together and unloaded: cycle the action several times, confirm the bolt locks open on the carrier stop and returns fully into battery, and check the front cap is tight and the choke seated. Short-stroking straight after a clean points at oil left in the gas system, which the book says should carry none.
